title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the notes study representations of a 'loop equation' (an equation in a fundamental group or braid-type group) into GL(M) with M of rank 2, given by sections such as rho, sigma and a unipotent eps_0 = 1 + N_0 with N_0^2 = 0. X_{rho,sigma} is a scheme attached to these data and on which a group acts. Its precise definition is on earlier pages and cannot be recovered from here. On the previous page Grothendieck computed that the natural homomorphism (66) from a group B~_0 to X_{rho,sigma} has kernel mu_2. This kernel comes from the centre G_m of GL(M): T_sigma ∩ T_rho = G_m, and G_m ∩ B~_0 consists of the scalars lambda with lambda^2 = 1.

On this page he concludes that (66) factors through a monomorphism (70): B~_0/mu_2 -> X_{rho,sigma}. He then remarks that B~_0 is not the 'right' group to use. In the model case eps_0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]] the stabiliser of the line spanned by N_0 is the Borel subgroup B_0 = {[[p,l],[0,q]] : pq invertible}. Such a u acts on N_0 by u N_0 u^{-1} = (p/q) N_0. The condition defining B~_0 is that this character chi(u) = p/q equals det u = pq, which gives q^2 = 1 (71). So B~_0 = {q = ±1}, which is B'_0 × mu_2.

The 'good' group is instead B'_0 = {[[p,l],[0,1]] : p invertible}, i.e. the affine group Aff_1, an extension of G_m by G_a. To state this without coordinates, he splits det on the Borel of the flag defined by N_0 into its two diagonal characters, det u = p(u) q(u) (72). The two are told apart by u N_0 u^{-1} = (p(u)/q(u)) N_0 (73). The good group is then cut out by q(u) = 1 (74), not by (71).

On the next page: B'_0 is smooth of dimension 2, sits in the exact sequence 1 -> L_0 (= G_a) -> B'_0 -> G_m -> 1, and meets the centre trivially. Hence B'_0 -> X_{rho,sigma} is a monomorphism. It is an isomorphism once surjectivity on geometric points is checked, which he leaves aside. Purpose: to identify the scheme X_{rho,sigma} for these 'loop equation' data in rank 2 with the affine group ax+b.
errors: No mathematical error. Note that B~_0 = {q = ±1} is canonically B'_0 × mu_2, so (70) B~_0/mu_2 ≅ B'_0 is consistent with (76). The 'good group' remark is a cosmetic normalisation, not a correction of an error.
Surjectivity of B'_0 -> X_{rho,sigma} on geometric points (needed for the isomorphism) is left unverified on the next page.

ideas.what: Stabiliser of a nilpotent N_0 up to scalar is the Borel; its two diagonal characters p, q are intrinsically separated by the action on N_0 (u N_0 u^{-1} = (p/q) N_0).
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup / adjoint action on the root space, characters of a torus
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general theory of roots and Borels)

ideas.what: Replacing the group B~_0 = B'_0 × mu_2 by the affine group B'_0 = Aff_1 (q = 1) so that the action on X_{rho,sigma} is free / a monomorphism, killing the central mu_2.
ideas.modern_name: affine group Aff_1 acting simply transitively on a moduli of rank-2 local system data

ideas.what: Monomorphism of smooth group schemes plus surjectivity on geometric points implies isomorphism ('principes généraux').

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-scheme bookkeeping (Borel characters, quotient by central mu_2, normalising to Aff_1) inside a larger unpublished computation. Nothing on this page itself is new.
transcription_corrections: First line reads 'en un monomorphisme' (continuing 'se factorise' from the previous page), not 'et un isomorphisme'.
(70) should be B~_0/mu_2 ↪ X_{rho,sigma}, a monomorphism.
The struck-out symbol after eps_0 is a crossed-out 'B...'.
The relation is χ'(u) = χ(u) with 'det u = pq' written beneath; 'pour une cellule invariante' is uncertain, possibly 'pour un élément u'.
'B♮_0' is likely B_0 (or B^#_0), the full Borel.

Next page: 'un groupe qui est libre (⊂ un cer. 2!)' is more likely 'lisse (de dim. 2!)'; the exact sequence is 1 -> L_0 -> B'_0 -> G_m -> 1 and should be numbered (75); G_lin is likely G_m (the centre).
